page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-44 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 44 dedicated vCPUs derived from 22 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 176 GB of system RAM, providing an even 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The processor architecture includes 105 MB of shared L3 cache and per-core L2 caches of 2 MB. It is equipped with advanced instruction sets including Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8) alongside AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators like VAES and SHA-NI. The server includes no bundled local disk storage or discrete GPUs, requiring attached network persistent disks for stateful workloads.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong performance in targeted computational tasks, notably in hardware encryption where the instance achieves a PassMark score of 38,725.32, ranking in the top tier. General multi-core throughput aligns with median cloud baselines, as reflected in a PassMark CPU score of 47,631.73 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 15,718.0. In memory throughput testing, the platform achieves 113.46 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads. Onboard AMX accelerators support effective CPU-based inference for smaller AI workloads, reaching 187.15 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 7B model. However, throughput drops sharply to 2.39 tokens per second for generation on 70B models, illustrating the CPU boundaries relative to dedicated hardware accelerators.

Resource allocation on the c3-standard-44 balances compute density against memory capacity, minimizing idle resource overhead for standard scalable tasks. The instance serves multi-threaded backend applications, large-scale web serving tiers, software compilation pipelines, and containerized microservice infrastructure. The lack of complimentary public IPv4 addresses and onboard NVMe storage necessitates external cloud infrastructure planning for network ingress and persistent data persistence.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-44 is a general-purpose virtual instance configured with 44 dedicated vCPUs across 22 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the server integrates 176 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside 105 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives. No local disk storage or discrete GPUs are bundled with this instance type. Benchmarks demonstrate solid cryptographic performance and stable median compute throughput, alongside capable small-to-medium CPU-based AI inference. The absence of local disk drives requires reliance on persistent network storage for stateful services. The instance is suited for multi-threaded backend applications, enterprise web serving, compilation pipelines, and container clusters.
